sources.citation: Beyer, Klaus & Janika Kunzmann. 2022. Retracing labial-velar consonants in Mbum (Adamawa): Between genetic transmission and language contact. Afrika und Übersee 95. doi:10.15460/auue.2022.95.1.270
sources.note: Nothing: a full-text search for stress/accent; no mention of Kare/Kari at all and no mention of stress or accent. Not a Kare source.

sources.citation: Elders, Stefan. 2006. Issues in comparative Kebi-Benue (Adamawa). Africana Linguistica 12: 37-88.
sources.note: Comparative phonology of the Mbum/Kebi-Benue group including Kare data (PHOIBLE's Kare inventory with tones H/M/L is taken from it); may carry a remark on prosody for the group. Open access on Persée but the PDF download is protected by an altcha proof-of-work challenge that automated download/direct download could not pass; a browser download is trivial.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, inventory 1347 'Kare' (GM source),https://phoible.org/inventories/view/1347;and Grambank,https://grambank.clld.org/languages/kare1338(source Lim 1997, coder Jakob Lesage); and Glottolog 5.3 languoid page kare1338
sources.note: Nothing on stress; PHOIBLE lists three level tones (˦ ˧ ˨) citing Elders 2006; Grambank and Glottolog only give sources and names (Kali, Kari, Karré, Kerɛ).

sources.citation: Wikipedia. Kare language (Adamawa).https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kare_language_(Adamawa) (phonology summarized from Lim 1997)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; reports only 'High and low tone' contrast, with rising or falling tones possible on monosyllabic words; autonym nzáà kã́rĩ́; dialects Kare (Kari, Kali) and Tale.

sources.citation: Meguieng, Sidze Sandrine. 2010. Aspect of the tonology of Kari according to the lexical phonology model. MA thesis, Université de Yaoundé I.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Modern tonological treatment of the Cameroon variety (Kari); a tonology thesis typically states whether the language has stress/accent in addition to tone. Yaoundé I MA theses are rarely online; no record found.
sources.venue: MA thesis, Université de Yaoundé I

tone.citation_as_reported: Meguieng, Sidze Sandrine. 2010. Aspect of the tonology of Kari according to the lexical phonology model. MA thesis, Université de Yaoundé I.

sources.citation: Lim, François. 1997. Description linguistique du Karé : phonologie, syntaxe. Thèse de doctorat, Université de la Sorbonne Nouvelle (Paris 3), dir. F. Cloarec-Heiss. 405 pp. ANRT microfiche reproduction, Lille, 1998 (ISBN 2-284-00671-X).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only; the linked copy is not accessible
sources.note: The only full description of the language; its phonology part (per SUDOC record and Wikipedia's summary of the tone system) is the most likely place for any statement on stress/accent vs tone. HathiTrust holds a search-only digitization (mdp.39015047495067); an ILL of the ANRT microfiche or a HathiTrust full-text term search from a browser (terms: accent, accentuation, intensité, tonème) would settle it.
sources.venue: Thèse de doctorat, Université de la Sorbonne Nouvelle (Paris 3), dir
